Turn one module's .Rmd into a book chapter

Source: R/LandR-related.R
prepOneModuleRmd.Rd

Copies <module>/<module>.Rmd to <stagingPath>/<module>2.Rmd and rewrites the copy. Nothing is written into the module's own directory. The steps, in order, because several depend on the one before:

Usage

prepOneModuleRmd(x, rebuildCache, stagingPath)

Arguments

x

path to the module's own .Rmd.

rebuildCache

passed through from prepManualRmds(); the value written into the chunk's cache.rebuild option.

stagingPath

directory the chapter is written into. The module's own directory is never written to; root.dir still points at it.

Value

the path of the <module>2.Rmd written.

Details

  1. strip the YAML header, so the chapter inherits the book's output format;

  2. add a chapter title if the module does not open with one;

  3. find the setup chunk, or synthesize one (ensureSetupChunk());

  4. force that chunk to eval = TRUE, cache = FALSE, so it runs again in the book even if the module set otherwise for standalone knitting;

  5. point root.dir at the module directory, injecting it if absent;

  6. set cache.rebuild from rebuildCache, injecting it if absent;

  7. move the References heading to the end, adding one if absent, and append the LaTeX \\printbibliography command.

Steps 5 and 6 both inject after the chunk header, so cache.rebuild ends up above root.dir in the generated chapter.
